page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-256GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs. The CPU allocation is shared, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core. This configuration does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 10% and single-threaded compression benchmarks ranking in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core and parallelized workloads perform significantly better. The PassMark CPU score, extended instructions test, encryption test, and physics test all rank in the top 25%. Additionally, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations demonstrate strong performance, placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is also strong, while large block read/write speeds and Geekbench multi-core scores remain in the average tier.

Because this server utilizes a shared CPU allocation, it offers a cost-efficient profile for high-density, multi-threaded workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core performance. The lack of local storage means storage must be attached externally, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This server is best suited for parallelized workloads such as multi-threaded data processing, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and general-purpose applications that can leverage its 64-core architecture without being bottlenecked by shared CPU limits or single-threaded execution speeds.
